steps: Choose the design option

Standard, Komfort Zone Kit (KZK-045) or Kozy Power Vent (#KPV): the choice sets framing, clearances, venting and which safety barriers are allowed. Minimum enclosure and ceiling height is 80" standard, 86" with KZK.

Decide before setting the appliance; framing, clearances and vent configuration depend on it.

  • Standard: follow the sections marked "standard installation". Fireplace chamber and ceiling at least 80" (2032mm). Only the Figure 2.2 barriers are allowed.
  • Komfort Zone Kit (KZK-045): redistributes radiant heat through a plenum; allows combustible facing above, heat reduction for a TV above and lower mantel clearances. Chamber and ceiling at least 86" (2184mm); framing, mantel and trim per the KZK manual. NK48-PSF and NK48-FRSF barriers are approved only with KZK. Remove the convection plates and insulation (Section 4.0, p. 21) before setting the unit.
  • Kozy Power Vent (#KPV): fan-powered mechanical draft, horizontal terminations only, usable with either option; it does not change facing, finishing or safety barrier requirements. System requirements are in the #KPV manual.

Approved in a bedroom; in an aftermarket, permanently located manufactured home (USA only) or mobile home where local codes allow; and in an outdoor covered area protected from direct precipitation (operation 40°F to 110°F; black painted barriers recommended outdoors).
Frame the enclosure

Frame to the Figure 3.4 rough-in (the same for every design option) on a level base that carries the fireplace and vent. Set it on wood or a non-combustible surface, or on a metal or wood panel the full width and depth.

Rough-in dimensions are shown only in Figure 3.4 (diagram, p. 16). The wall pass-through height is in Figure 3.6, measured with a Simpson DuraVent elbow; elbow heights vary, so adjust the opening to keep clearances. Clearances assume nominal 2" × 4" framing.

  • Not directly on carpeting, vinyl, tile or other combustibles other than wood flooring. Above floor level, build a solid, continuous platform.
  • Allow for wall covering and facing thickness. Masonry needs a foundation for the full load and a lintel over the top.
  • Insulate outside walls of the chase (cold air transfer area).
  • If possible, position the unit so the vent terminates between two studs.
  • Leave room in front for barrier removal, gas line installation and service access.
  • TV above: KZK is highly recommended. The allowed TV recess is 4-1/4" (108mm), from the front of the 2x4 framing to the back of the pocket finishing material.
Attach the finishing trim kit
The included NK48-FTK trim is recommended and must be attached before the fireplace is installed. Fit the top trim panel before the top stand-offs and nailing flanges.

The trim gives finishing material a metal edge to butt against and ensures the safety barrier fits. Kit: (2) side pieces, (1) bottom piece, (1) top piece.

  1. Remove and save the screws holding the side heat shields and the nailing flanges.
  2. Fit the side trim pieces; reinstall the heat shields and nailing flanges on top of them with the saved screws.
  3. Remove the top stand-off screws, build the top stand-off assembly on top of the top trim piece, align with the front stand-off holes and secure.
  4. If fitted, remove and discard the existing bottom front frame portion; slot the new bottom trim piece into the bottom corners.
Stand-offs, flanges, set the unit
Form and attach the top stand-offs (8" to the header, non-combustible zone the full width) and the nailing flanges (9/16" to side framing). Set the fireplace flush with the framing and secure it.

Stand-offs must be formed and attached before the fireplace goes into the opening. With KZK-045, finish its preparation first.

Top stand-offs (Section 3.5)

  1. Remove and save the (2) screws holding the stand-off heat shields and brackets on top.
  2. Bend each bracket at the perforations; align with the holes in the top and secure with the saved screws plus the (2) on top of the fireplace.
  3. Form the heat shields (flange up and to the back) and secure with the (8) screws from the components packet.

Nailing flanges (Section 3.6)

  1. Remove the (2) flanges from the sides and mount them on the outside corners, stand-off flanges facing away from the fireplace.
  2. Bend at the perforation until parallel with the fireplace face, never toward it.
  3. Set the stud against the small stand-off on the back of the flange; secure with nails or screws.
Use only non-combustible material in the header zone (no wood or sheetrock). Never permanently remove the nailing flange assemblies; they must be secured whatever the finish material.
Gas line + leak test

Connect a listed 1/2" tee-handle manual shut-off and flexible connector to the 1/2" control valve inlet; a 3/8" × 24" flexible connector and shut-off valve come with the fireplace. Check every connection for leaks with soapy water.

Run the line in through the gas line hole to the connection point (gas line access is shown in Figure 2.1, a diagram on p. 9). Don't route it where it would obstruct the fan.

  • Qualified person only, to local codes or ANSI Z223.1; Massachusetts: a licensed plumber or gas fitter.
  • Built for natural gas. For propane, follow the conversion kit instructions; the stepper motor is sold separately. Convert before installing light kit components or the log set.
  • Supply-piping tests above 1/2 psi (3.5 kPa): disconnect the appliance and its shut-off valve. At or below 1/2 psi: isolate it by closing its manual shut-off valve.
  • Check all connections, field or factory made, with soapy water.
  • High altitude: consult the local gas distributor or authority having jurisdiction for rating methods.
Install the vent

Run an approved 5" × 8" co-axial system (or reduce to 4" × 6-5/8") within the listed vertical, horizontal and combination limits, with 1/4" rise per 12" on horizontal sections. Hold the Table 3.1 vent clearances and the Table 7.1 termination clearances.

Vent runs and limits are under the Venting spec card. Requirements apply to natural gas and propane.

  • Provide a way to visually check the vent connection after the fireplace is installed.
  • Flexible vent pipe only outside the appliance enclosure, and never to terminate the system.
  • Never connect to a chimney flue serving a separate solid-fuel appliance.
  • Restrictor plate (components packet; 2 knock-out inner rings, most restriction with both intact): fit per Figure 8.1 before attaching the vent, or later through the baffle.
  • Horizontal: wall thimbles that keep the required top clearance; never recess the cap into the wall or siding. Vinyl or PVC siding can deform from cap heat; ask the vent maker about siding protectors.
  • Attic insulation shields and wall thimbles may be insulated with unfaced insulation listed non-combustible per ASTM E 136.

Termination clearances (Table 7.1, natural draft)

A · above grade, veranda, porch, deck, balcony12" (30cm)
B · window or door that may be opened9" (23cm) US · 12" (30cm) Canada
J · non-mechanical air inlet9" (23cm) US · 12" (30cm) Canada
K · mechanical air inlet3' (91cm) above US · 6' (1.83m) Canada
N / O · between two terminations12" (30cm)

The rest of Table 7.1 (soffits, corners, meter and regulator, sidewalks) is on p. 34; several rows defer to local codes and the gas supplier. A vent shall not terminate directly above a sidewalk or paved driveway that is located between two single family dwellings and serves both dwellings (Table 7.1 footnote †). Massachusetts: 10' (3m) above a mechanical inlet within 10' horizontally. Clearances are to heat-resistant materials, not vinyl soffits, ceilings or overhangs.
Electrical
Bring 120VAC, 60Hz, 6 Amps that is hot at all times, with no switch in the supply. Plug the three-prong cord into a properly grounded receptacle and ground to local codes, ANSI/NFPA 70 or CSA C22.1.
Bulbs, logs, glass, barrier

Convert to propane first if needed. Fit the 5 halogen bulbs in the front bottom light kit (not factory-installed), place the log set per its own instructions, refit the glass and hang the safety barrier.

• Disconnect all electric power first. Handle halogen bulbs with a soft cloth, never bare hands.
  • Front bottom light kit: lift out the log rack/ember media tray ((4) screws) and fit the (5) bulbs from the components packet. Back bottom and top light kits come with bulbs installed (replacement steps on p. 44).
  • Logs: Traditional (NK48-500) or Birch (NK48-B501), per the instructions with the set. Install any panel set first.
  • Glass: set the bottom slots on the rails, tilt the top in, pull the (2) spring-loaded latches out and up.
  • Safety barrier (Section 5.3, p. 30): center it over the glass frame with the brackets inside the air openings, then lower the notched tabs into the slots, checking the depth suits the finish material. On NK48-RSVF, NK48-PSVF, NK48-PSF and NK48-FRSF the louver notch must match the notched-tab position.
The barrier must be installed. The bottom of the fireplace must be level with the finished hearth for it to fit.
Initialize the controls

Rocker switch OFF, 4 AA in the backup holder, 3 AAA in the remote, AC connected, packaging out of the firebox. Press the sync button (3 beeps, amber LED), then the remote's ON/OFF within 5 seconds (4 beeps), and set the rocker switch to ON.

1. Set the ON/OFF rocker switch to OFF. Install (4) AA batteries (not included) in the control module's backup holder and the (3) AAA from the components packet in the remote. Connect the IFC module to AC power.
  2. Remove all packaging and combustibles from the firebox. The next steps spark the pilot repeatedly and light it if gas is supplied.
  3. Lift off the safety barrier, remove the bottom frame piece (Section 9.2) and slide out the control module to reach the remote sync button.
  4. Press the sync button: (3) beeps and an amber LED.
  5. Within (5) seconds press ON/OFF on the remote: (4) beeps, and the pilot lights.
  6. Press ON/OFF again: the pilot goes out. The control system is initialized.
  7. Rocker switch to ON for remote operation; reinstall the bottom frame (it maintains clearances) and the barrier.

Pilot mode: with the system off, press Mode to the CPI icon; up arrow = CPI, down arrow = IPI. For manual operation without the remote, hold the sync button for (3) beeps and press it again within (5) seconds; the rocker switch then runs the main burner, on HI only.
Check pressures & tune the flame
Verify inlet and manifold pressures at the valve's IN and OUT taps. After 15 minutes of burn, adjust the venturis or the restrictor plate if the flames lift, soot or flicker.

Pressure test steps are under the Inlet and Manifold spec cards (Tables 12.1–12.2). Venturi air shutters are factory set; venturi adjustment must be done by a qualified service technician, in slight increments, with the fireplace cooled.

Dark orange flame, black tipsVenturi closed too far · open slightly
Short, blue flamesVenturi open too far · close slightly
Lifting (ghosting) flamesGas pressure too high and/or venturi closed too far · check manometer, open slightly
Short, flickeringExcessive draft · add restrictor plate
Lifting or ghosting (draft)Insufficient draft · remove inner ring(s) or the restrictor plate

Restrictor: remove the barrier, glass frame, refractory (if installed) and logs, then the (4) baffle screws. Bend the tabs to about 80° and insert the plate into the 5" (127mm) exhaust, tabs toward you. Vertical terminations may show an active, compact flame.

Factory venturi openings: NG left/right 1/16" (1.5mm), rear 5/16" (8mm); LP left/right 1/4" (6mm), rear 5/16" (8mm).

If flames still lift or ghost after opening the restrictor and verifying the vent installation, shut off the gas supply and call a qualified service technician.

panels.title: Pilot won't light or stay lit
items: Power interrupted → restore it, or run on fully charged backup batteries
Wiring disconnected → check every connection against the wiring schematic
Gas off → check all shut-offs between appliance and main line; empty propane tank → refill
Low gas pressure (bent line, too-narrow pipe, low line pressure) → plumber or gas supplier
Pilot adjustment screw not sealed → seal it; don't over-tighten
Pilot not reaching the rectification sensor → it must envelop the sensor top and reach the burner
Pilot always on → control set to CPI; set it to IPI

panels.title: Burner won't light or no response
items: ON/OFF rocker switch in OFF → switch it ON
Gas off, low supply or empty propane tank → verify supply; refill
Faulty or incorrect wiring → check against Figures 10.1–10.3
Plugged burner orifice → remove blockage; pilot must be directed to ignite the burner
No call for heat → remote powered ON, thermostat operation OFF
No reaction → replace remote or backup batteries; reprogram the remote to the IFC module
Maximum failed ignitions or flame restorations reached → reset the IFC module

panels.title: Pilot & burner go out while running
items: Glass assembly installed incorrectly (Section 9.1)
Vent cap installed incorrectly or blocked → adjust; remove debris
Horizontal vent without 1/4" rise per 12" of travel
Exhaust leaking back into the firebox → find and repair
Excessive draft → install or modify the restrictor plate

panels.title: Soot on glass, or blue lifting flames
items: Soot: improper log placement → reset per the log set instructions
Soot: venturi air shutters too closed → open slightly
Blue flame lifting off burner: venturi too open → close slightly
Vent cap installed incorrectly or blocked, or vent pipes leaking → adjust, repair, remove debris

codes: Backup pack below 4V; double-beep on ON/OFF. Replace the batteries.
No flame after both tries. Verify gas is on and the sensor isn't shorted; reset or re-initialize (11.2).

light.title: Turning the fireplace on and off
light.html:
Your fireplace lights itself with an electric spark when you press a key on the remote. There's no match and no knob to hold.

  1. Check that the ON/OFF rocker switch is on. It sits behind the safety screen, on the left side, and it must be on for the remote to run the fireplace.
  2. Press the ON/OFF key on the remote. The fireplace beeps once to confirm.
  3. About 4 seconds later the control starts sparking to light the pilot, and the pilot lights the main burner.
  4. Set the flame height with the up and down arrows.

To turn it off, press ON/OFF again. You'll hear one beep and the burner goes out.

If it doesn't light

The control tries twice. Each try sparks for about 60 seconds, with about 35 seconds of rest in between. If both fail, it locks out and a red light blinks 3 times, over and over. Make sure the gas is turned on. Then reset it: press ON/OFF, wait about 2 seconds, and press it again. Switching the rocker switch off, then on after 2 seconds, also starts it over.

If you smell gas, don't try to light it. Leave the building right away. Immediately call your gas supplier from a neighbor's phone. See "Safety and gas smell."

remote.title: Using the remote
remote.html:
The Proflame 2 remote runs everything. The fireplace answers each command with a single beep.

The keys

  • ON/OFF turns the fireplace on and off.
  • Up and down arrows step through 6 flame levels. Keep pressing down and the flame turns off; press up while it's off and it relights on high.
  • Mode moves between the icons for the fan, the top light and the ember-bed light. Then use the arrows on the one you picked.
  • Thermostat starts the thermostat, below.

Thermostat and smart mode

Press the thermostat key once. The screen shows the room temperature and your set temperature; change the setting with the arrows. Keep pressing until "SMART" appears and the remote adjusts the flame height for you, turning it down as the room reaches your setting. In smart mode you can't change the flame by hand.

Two handy extras

  • Key lock: press Mode and the up arrow together. A lock icon appears. Do it again to unlock.
  • °F or °C: with the fireplace off, press Thermostat and Mode together.
The remote takes 3 AAA batteries in the bay at its base. A battery icon on the screen means they're running low.

sounds.title: Beeps, pauses and other normal behavior
sounds.html:
Beeps

  • One beep: your remote command was received.
  • A double beep when you press ON/OFF: the backup batteries are low. The fireplace won't take commands until you replace them.
  • 3 beeps, then 4 beeps: the remote is being paired to the fireplace, which happens at setup.

It turned off by itself for a few seconds

When the pilot has stayed lit, the system turns itself off for about 5 seconds within 24 hours to run a safety check. Then it goes back to whatever you last asked for. That's normal.

The pilot went out on its own

On continuous pilot, if the main burner hasn't lit for 7 days in a row, the pilot turns off. It's a standard safety feature.

Blue flames at first

When the fireplace is first lit, the flames look blue and gradually turn yellow over the first 15 minutes. If they stay blue, or turn dark orange with black tips, have a qualified service technician check the burner air settings.

Ticks and creaks

Some minor expansion, contraction or movement of parts makes noise. The warranty calls that normal, not a defect.

glass.title: Cleaning the glass
glass.html:
Cleaning the glass is a once-a-year job you can do yourself. Wait until the fireplace is completely cool.

  1. Clear a flat, stable surface big enough to lay the glass frame on.
  2. Lift the safety screen up and out of its slots.
  3. Pull the 2 spring-loaded latches at the top of the firebox out and up. Tilt the top of the glass toward you and lift it off the 2 rails at the bottom.
  4. Clean it with a fireplace glass cleaner and a soft cloth. Don't use abrasive cleaners, and take care not to scratch it.
  5. Set the slots on the bottom of the frame onto the rails, tilt the top into place, and pull the latches out and up to lock it. Put the safety screen back on.
Never clean the glass while it's hot, strike or slam it, or run the fireplace with the glass removed, cracked or broken, or without the safety screen.

A cracked or damaged glass assembly is replaced as a complete unit (part 701-067T) by a qualified service person. Wear protective gloves if you have to handle broken glass.

modes.title: Continuous or on-demand pilot
modes.html:
Your fireplace can run its pilot flame two ways. You choose with the remote.

IPI · on demandThe control sparks the pilot each time the fireplace turns on
CPI · continuousA standing pilot that stays lit even with the burner off

A standing pilot keeps the firebox warm and starts a draft in the vent, so the main burner lights with less disruption to the air flow.

To switch

  1. Turn the fireplace off.
  2. Press Mode until the CPI mode icon is selected.
  3. Press the up arrow for CPI, or the down arrow to go back to IPI. One beep confirms it.

With the fireplace on, a snowflake icon on the remote's screen means CPI is on. No snowflake means IPI.

Pilot won't go out? That's CPI; set it to IPI if you don't want a standing pilot. On CPI the pilot also turns off after 7 days in a row without the main burner lighting. Lighting the burner at any point in those 7 days restarts the count.

fan.title: Fan and accent lights
fan.html:
The fan and the lights run from the remote. Press Mode to move to an icon, then use the arrows. One beep confirms each change.

FanOff, or 6 speeds
Top accent light6 brightness levels
Ember-bed light (AUX icon)Up arrow on, down arrow off

Why the fan waits

In thermostat mode the fan waits 5 minutes after the fireplace lights, so heat can build first, and keeps running for about 12 minutes after the fireplace turns off. In manual mode it runs at its last setting, with no delay starting or stopping.

Ember-bed brightness

Lift the safety screen up and out. The light's adjustment knob is underneath the firebox: turn it clockwise for brighter, counterclockwise for dimmer. Put the screen back when you're done.

The ember-bed light is an auxiliary function that may first need switching on in the remote, using a key sequence in the manual.

In a power outage the fan and lights don't work. The flames still do, on the backup batteries.

power.title: Power outages and batteries
power.html:
The fireplace runs on 120-volt house power, with a battery pack in the control module as backup.

Backup pack (control module)4 × AA (not included)
Remote3 × AAA (included)

When the power goes out

The fireplace switches to the backup pack. The burner and flame height keep working; the fan and accent lights don't.

Low-battery signs

  • Backup pack: a double beep when you press ON/OFF, and a red light that blinks once, over and over. After that it ignores commands until you put in fresh batteries. It beeps once when it has power again.
  • Remote: a battery icon shows on the screen before the power runs out, and goes away once you replace them.

How long batteries last depends on their quality and how often the fireplace lights.

Remote not responding? Put fresh batteries in both places first. If that doesn't help, the remote may need to be reprogrammed to the control module, a job for a qualified technician.

safety.title: Safety and gas smell
safety.html:
If you smell gas

  • Don't try to light any appliance.
  • Don't touch any electrical switch, and don't use any phone in your building.
  • Leave the building right away.
  • Immediately call your gas supplier from a neighbor's phone and follow their instructions. If you can't reach them, call the fire department.

Every day

  • The glass gets hot. The safety screen in front of it reduces the risk of burns for children and others at risk, so keep it on. If it's damaged, replace it with Hussong Mfg.'s barrier for this fireplace.
  • Keep furniture, draperies and anything that burns away from the fireplace. Never store or use gasoline or other flammable vapors or liquids nearby.
  • Don't run it with the glass removed, cracked or broken.
  • The remote's key lock helps prevent unsupervised use.
Been under water? Don't use the fireplace if any part has been under water. Call a qualified service technician right away to inspect it and replace any control or gas part that was under water.

service.title: Annual service
service.html:
Have the fireplace inspected before use and at least once a year by a professional service person. It may need cleaning more often if carpeting, bedding or similar materials shed a lot of lint nearby.

What the yearly service covers

  • Vacuuming the firebox, burner system and fan. The fan's bearings are sealed and need no oil.
  • Checking that the bottom latch assembly moves freely, with spring tension.
  • Examining the vent and vent cap for soot or blockage, and making sure combustion and ventilation air can flow.
  • Leak-checking the gas tubes and connections, and watching the pilot and burner run. Flames should be steady, not lifting or floating.
  • Testing the safety system: the main burner must light within 4 seconds of the gas valve opening, and the flame-failure shutoff must act within 30 seconds.
  • Inspecting the glass for cracks, scratches and nicks.

Your part

Clean the glass once a year (see Clean the glass) and keep the area around the fireplace clear of anything that burns. Any screen or barrier taken off for service must go back on before you use the fireplace.

warranty.title: Warranty at a glance
warranty.html:
Hussong Mfg. warrants your Kozy Heat fireplace to the original purchaser, from the date of purchase, against defects in materials and workmanship at the time of manufacture.

30 days · parts and laborPaint, light bulbs, gasket material, glass media and media dam
Year 1 · parts and laborAll other parts and material, subject to the exclusions
Years 2 through lifetime · parts onlyFirebox, heat exchanger, logs, burner tube or pan, outer shell, heat shield(s), front viewing glass (thermal shock only), refractory firebox liner (excluding enamel and glass panels)

Labor is reimbursed to an authorized dealer only. You don't need to send in any registration; keep your proof of purchase with the date, serial number and model. If you notice a defect, contact your authorized dealer within 30 days.

What voids or limits it

  • Installation by anyone but a licensed, authorized service technician or contractor, or not following the manual.
  • Removing the serial number or testing label, or altering the fireplace in any way.
  • Submersion in water, or long periods of dampness or condensation.
  • It isn't transferable, and it doesn't cover normal wear, venting or environmental problems, or non-Hussong parts.
This is a summary. The full terms and exclusions are in the manual.

High altitude

US: above 2,000' (610m), reduce input ratings 4% for each 1,000' (305m) above sea level. Canada: above 4,500' (1,372m), reduce the certified high-altitude rating 4% for each additional 1,000' (305m). Listed to CSA 2.17 for high altitudes.

specInlet.title: Inlet (supply) pressure
specInlet.html:
Natural gas5" WC min · 10" WC max
NG recommended7" WC
Propane11" WC min · 13" WC max

Measure at the valve tap marked IN (A in Figure 12.1), with all other gas appliances in the house on, at full capacity.

  1. Loosen the IN tap screw counter-clockwise; attach a manometer with a 1/4" (6mm) I.D. hose.
  2. Light pilot and burner; the reading must be between the minimum and maximum (Table 12.1).
  3. Turn burner and pilot off, remove the hose and turn the screw clockwise until snug. Don't over-tighten.
  4. Relight and reattach the manometer to confirm the tap is sealed: it should read no pressure.
If inlet pressure is too high or too low, contact the gas company; only a qualified gas service technician should adjust incoming pressure. For supply-piping tests above 1/2 psi (3.5 kPa), disconnect the appliance and its shut-off valve.

specManifold.title: Manifold pressure
specManifold.html:
Natural gas · high / low3.5" / 1.6" WC
Propane · high / low10" / 6.4" WC

Measure at the valve tap marked OUT (B in Figure 12.1).

  1. Light the pilot. Loosen the OUT tap screw counter-clockwise and attach the manometer with a 1/4" (6mm) I.D. hose.
  2. Light the burner and compare the reading with Table 12.2.
  3. Turn burner and pilot off, remove the hose and turn the screw clockwise until snug. Don't over-tighten.
  4. Reattach the manometer to confirm the seal: no pressure with pilot and burner on.

kPa as printed: NG 0.87 / 0.40 kPa; LP 2.49 / 1.59 kPa.

specVent.title: Venting
specVent.html:
5" (127mm) exhaust by 8" (203mm) air intake co-axial pipe; may be reduced to 4" × 6-5/8" with a vent reducer from an approved system. Approved makers, horizontal and vertical: American Metal Products (Ameri-Vent), BDM, ICC, Metal Fab, Olympia Chimney Supply, Selkirk and Simpson DuraVent (cap part numbers in Tables 8.1 and 8.2). Kozy Power Vent #KPV is also approved; its manual covers power-vent layouts.

Natural-draft runs · NG and LP

Vertical3' (914mm) min / 50' (15.24m) max + cap
Vertical with 4" × 6-5/8" reducer3' min / 50' max; any 45° elbow needs a 10' (3.05m) minimum vertical run; up to (4) 45°, no 90°
12" vertical + 90°Up to 24" (610mm) horizontal
24" vertical + 90°Up to 8' (2.44m) horizontal
36" vertical + 90°Up to 12' (3.66m) horizontal
25' max vertical + 90°Up to 25' (7.62m) horizontal
Basement36" min 5" × 8" vertical + 4" × 6-5/8" reducer + 90° + up to 24" horizontal

Each minimum-horizontal layout is the vertical pipe + 90° elbow + cap. Combination runs: 25' max vertical + 25' max horizontal = 50' (15.2m) total, terminating inside the shaded area of Figure 8.7 (a diagram, p. 41). Up to (5) 90° elbows, subtracting 3' (914mm) for each 90° after the first; (2) 45° may replace (1) 90°, subtracting 18" (457mm) per 45°. Reduced vertical runs also lose 18" per 45°.

Propane only: on minimum-horizontal 5" × 8" venting and when reduced to 4" × 6-5/8", set the left and right burner venturis to 3/8" (10mm) (p. 8; marked on the layouts on p. 39).

Class A / masonry chimney conversion

4" aluminum flexible exhaust (listed vent makers) inside an existing Class A metal or masonry chimney of at least 7" ID: 4" × 6-5/8" reducer + retro connector + 10' (3.05m) min / 50' (15.24m) max of 4" flex + top adapter + cap, with 0" to 24" (610mm) of horizontal run. Install the vent heat shield assembly with minimum horizontal venting off the top, and avoid tight bends. Have the chimney inspected first and confirm local approval.

specClear.title: Clearances to combustibles
specClear.html:
Standard installation, Table 3.1, based on nominal 2" × 4" framing. The Komfort Zone Kit (KZK-045) changes these; use its manual.

Min. enclosure height80" (2032mm) · 86" (2184mm) with KZK-045
Base of fireplace to ceiling80" (2032mm)
Fireplace top to ceiling39" (991mm)
Top, side and back stand-offs0" (0mm)
Fireplace corners1" (25mm)
Fireplace front36" (914mm)
Fireplace sides to adjacent sidewall1" (25mm)
Note: p. 14 (Table 3.1) and p. 23 give a 1" (25mm) sidewall clearance from the side of the fireplace; the figure note on p. 27 says a 3/4" (19mm) sidewall clearance is shown from the side of the fireplace, with 0" to the side of the finishing trim kit when installed.

The top stand-offs provide the 8" (203mm) minimum to the header; only non-combustible material in that zone, the full width of the fireplace. The nailing flanges provide the 9/16" (14mm) minimum from the sides to framing.

Vent pipe inside the enclosure (Table 3.1)

Horizontal · top surface15-7/8" (403mm)
Horizontal · left, right, bottom1" (25mm)
Vertical · all surfaces1" (25mm)

Both figures are minimums. Inside the fireplace chamber, horizontal pipe needs 15-7/8" (403mm) from the top of the chamber (p. 14, p. 17). After the wall pass-through, horizontal pipe needs 1" (25mm) on all surfaces (p. 17), and p. 37's venting requirements give a 1" (25mm) minimum on the top, sides and bottom of horizontal vent pipe, with wall thimbles that keep the required clearances wherever it passes through a wall.

specMantel.title: Mantel, hearth and facing
specMantel.html:
Standard installation with barriers NK48-PSVF, NK48-RSVF, NK48A-MSF or NK48R-MSF. With NK48-PSF or NK48-FRSF (KZK installs), use the KZK-045 manual.

3/4" (19mm) mantel trim9" (229mm) from top · 50" (1270mm) from base
6" (152mm) deep mantel12-1/2" (317mm) from top · 53-1/2" (1359mm) from base
Deeper mantels+1" (25mm) depth per 1" (25mm) of height, starting at the 6" mantel
8" non-combustible mantelFrom 41-3/4" (1060mm) above the base
Floor protectionNot required; combustible hearth allowed

Combustible flooring may run under the fireplace, allowing an unlimited combustible hearth projection; the hearth can't be raised above the base of the fireplace. An 8" non-combustible surround may sit flush with the trim kit's side and top edges (1" up for every 1" deeper). Mantel legs follow the sidewall clearance (see the Clearances note).

Non-combustible zone and finishing

  • A 50-1/4" × 8-3/4" non-combustible board is supplied and covers more than the minimum; the minimum zone is shown only in Figure 5.5 (a diagram in Section 5.1).
  • Non-combustible materials must meet ASTM E 136. Paper-faced gypsum (including Type X) and WonderBoard are not non-combustible.
  • Use heat-resilient tape, mesh and joint compound (such as Durabond) and a high-quality acrylic latex primer and finish; avoid flat or light-colored paints.
  • No one-piece U-shaped marble or stone; stone must tolerate temperatures greater than 160°F.

specElec.title: Electrical
specElec.html:
Supply (junction box)120VAC, 60Hz, 6 Amps
Backup battery pack4 × AA (not included)
Remote3 × AAA (included)
  • The AC supply must be hot at all times, with no switch in it. Shut off the household breaker before working on it.
  • Three-prong grounding plug into a properly grounded three-prong receptacle; never cut or remove the ground prong. Ground to local codes or, absent them, ANSI/NFPA 70 or CSA C22.1.
  • On battery backup the burner and flame modulation work; fan and lights don't.
  • Wiring diagrams are Figures 10.1–10.3 (pp. 47–49). Label all wires before disconnecting controls.
  • Outdoor covered installations: all wiring to the outdoor requirements of NECA NFPA 70.
Don't use the fireplace if any part has been under water; a qualified service technician must inspect it and replace any control-system part and gas control that was under water.

conflicts.issue: Sidewall clearance: 1" (25mm) from the side of the fireplace in Table 3.1 (p. 14) and Section 5.1.1 (p. 23), but the figure note on p. 27 says 3/4" (19mm) is shown from the side of the fireplace (0" to the side of the finishing trim kit when installed).

Top clearance on horizontal vent pipe: 15-7/8" (403mm) within the fireplace enclosure in Table 3.1 (p. 14) and Section 3.9.2 (p. 17, which applies 1" after the wall pass-through), but Section 8.2 (p. 37) states 1" (25mm) on the top, sides and bottom of horizontal vent pipe without distinguishing; p. 17's first bullet also says 1" from the top surface.
conflicts.reason: All are minimums, and p. 17 itself places them, listing both in one set of bullets: 15-7/8" (403mm) from the top of the chamber for horizontal pipe inside the fireplace chamber (matching Table 3.1, p. 14) and 1" (25mm) on all surfaces after the wall pass-through. p. 37's 1" (25mm) on the top, sides and bottom is the general venting minimum, stated with the wall-thimble rule; pipe that meets the in-chamber 15-7/8" also meets it. The guide now states both zones plainly.

review.notes: Checked against the catalog: NG 48,000/32,000 and LP 48,000/39,000 Btu/h, 5 x 8 venting, IPI/CPI selectable ignition and manufactured/mobile home approval all match (pp. 1, 8, 35, 54). Not checkable from the text: efficiency (no efficiency figure anywhere in the manual text), height/width/depth (dimensions are Figure 2.1, a drawing on p. 9 with no text), 315 lb weight, view area, and whether the fan kit is standard. The replacement glass with gasket is listed as 43-1/4" x 34-5/8" (701-067T, p. 69), smaller than the catalog view area of 44-1/2" x 35-3/8"; worth checking. Figure-only content not transcribed: rough-in (Fig. 3.4, p. 16), wall pass-through (Fig. 3.6), gas line access (Fig. 2.1), combination-venting shaded area (Fig. 8.7, p. 41), non-combustible zone (Fig. 5.5), barrier figures 2.2/2.3, wiring (Figs. 10.1-10.3, pp. 47-49), and p. 50 (Operating Instructions opener, no text beyond the heading). Section headings 11.1-11.6 are missing from the p. 51 text (the TOC puts them all on p. 51); the manual-operation steps (11.3 per the TOC) are introduced by 'To select the preferred pilot ignition feature,', apparently a copy error, so the guide describes them as manual operation. LP maximum inlet is 3.23 kPa on p. 8 but 3.24 kPa in Table 12.1 (p. 58); inch values agree (13" WC) and only inch values are used. The 3/8" venturi note on p. 59 omits the 'propane only' qualifier given on p. 8 and p. 39; the guide follows p. 8/p. 39 and says so. The 3/8" x 24" supplied connector vs the 1/2" shut-off/valve inlet (p. 31) is shown as printed. Manual cross-references are off: p. 35 cites Section 8.6 on page 41 (it is p. 42); troubleshooting cites 12.3.3 Vent Restriction (12.2.3) and 9.5 Log Set (9.4); p. 67 cites 9.6 Control Board (9.5). Text has lost ti/ft/tt ligatures, so find_in_manual misses words such as 'installation' or 'battery'. KZK-045 and KPV requirements live in separate kit manuals not provided.
